The stories show sign-in, forgot password and a two-step reset (the server checks the code, then the new password follows the rules).

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description:
A code block with shiki syntax highlighting, for docs and AI chat UIs. `<CodeBlock code={code} language="tsx" />` is complete on its own.

### Parts

- **`CodeBlockHeader`**: the chrome — `CodeBlockTitle`, `CodeBlockLanguage`, `CodeBlockWrapToggle`, `CodeBlockCopyButton`, `CodeBlockDownloadButton`.
- **`CodeBlockExpandButton`**: with `maxLines`.
- **`CodeBlockContent`**: to place inside your own scroll container.
- **`CodeBlockLineActions`**: one action group on the hovered or focused line.

A pinned copy button stays put while the code scrolls.

### Highlighting

shiki loads lazily on the first highlight (JavaScript regex engine, no WebAssembly) through the `code-block-highlight` lib. Pass `lines` from `highlightCode()` in a server loader, or `highlight={false}`, to never load it. Light and dark token colors switch with the theme.

### Lines

- **Marking**: `showLineNumbers`/`startLine`, `highlightedLines`/`highlightedWords`/`focusedLines` (line specs like `"2-4,7"`), `diff` and `lineLevels` — or shiki `transformers`.
- **`streaming`**: grows the code with a caret and stick-to-bottom, re-rendering only changed lines.
- **`foldable`**: folds by indentation.
- **`selectable`**: turns lines into a multi-select listbox.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

meta.origin: reui.io (https://reui.io/docs/components/base/code-block, MIT); buttons rebuilt on react-aria Button

items.name: code-block-highlight
items.title: Code Block Highlight
items.description:
The code block's shiki engine and pure helpers, with no `"use client"`, so a server loader can call it.

- **`highlightCode(code, options)`**: returns plain-JSON `CodeBlockLine[]` — dual light/dark token colors, line state from props or shiki transformers, and unchanged lines reused so streaming re-renders one row.
- **Loading**: shiki loads lazily on the JavaScript regex engine (no WebAssembly), one chunk per language from the static `codeBlockLanguages` map and per theme from `codeBlockThemes` (`github-light`/`github-dark`, or `css-variables` for design-token colors).
- **Helpers**: `parseLineSpec` (`"2-4,7"`), `markdownFences`/`markdownCodeProps` for AI transcripts, `ansiToLines` for terminal output, `parseUnifiedDiff` for git patches and `stripNotationComments`.

items.description:
A list edited in place inside a form: the user adds an item and fills it right there (payment methods, lots, recipients).

Rows, state and validation stay in the app (`useFieldArray`'s `fields`, `append`, `remove`).

- **`CollectionField`**: takes the `label` (a legend), `description`, the list's `error`, `itemCount`, `onAdd` and `addLabel`. `minItems` removes the remove buttons at the minimum, `maxItems` swaps the add button for a note once reached, and an empty list shows `emptyMessage`.
- **`CollectionFieldItem`**: `label` is numbered ("Lot 2") and also names its remove button; `onRemove` removes it. Two layouts: `row` for a few fields side by side on wide screens, with the remove button at the end; `group` for many fields under a visible legend with a static border, so items stay apart when fields stack on small screens.
- **`CollectionFieldSummary`** with **`CollectionFieldSummaryItem`**: the total, what is allocated and what remains (`isEmphasized`: by size and weight, with the state in words).
- **Focus**: adding announces the new item and focuses its first field; removing announces it and focuses the add button.

Lists filled elsewhere and only shown here (edited in a dialog, listed in a table) are a composition of `data-grid`/`item` and `dialog`, not this block.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.

items.name: color-contrast
items.title: Color Contrast
items.description:
WCAG 2 contrast helpers over OKLCH. Results are oklch strings clamped to sRGB.

- **Ratio**: contrast ratio and level.
- **`passingRanges`**: the ranges of any OKLCH, HSL, HSB or RGB channel where a color passes against a background.
- **`passingRegion`**: the passing part of a 2D color area, such as chroma × lightness.
- **`nearestContrastColor`**: the nearest passing color that keeps its hue.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.description:
A composable color picker: `ColorPicker` holds the color and shares it with parts laid out in any way.

Without children, `ColorPicker` is a swatch that opens the default panel in a popover.

### Parts

- **`ColorPickerTrigger`** + **`ColorPickerContent`**: a popover.
- **`ColorPickerPanel`**: a column of controls, or a standalone inline picker.
- **`ColorPickerArea`**: OKLCH chroma × lightness at the hue (the part sRGB can't show is left blank), or HSB saturation × brightness.
- **`ColorPickerWheel`**: a hue ring whose children fill the square inside it.
- **`ColorPickerSlider`**: any channel of OKLCH, HSL, HSB or RGB, or alpha; horizontal or vertical, painted with the colors it reaches.
- **`ColorPickerFields`**: a format menu with hex or per-channel fields; `ColorPickerChannelInput` for a single channel.
- **`ColorPickerInput`**: a text field taking any CSS color (Escape reverts), with a swatch that opens the popover against it.
- **`ColorPickerSwatches`**: presets, Tailwind's palette by default; `ColorPickerSwatch` for one.
- **Extras**: `ColorPickerValue`, `ColorPickerCopy`, `ColorPickerEyeDropper`, `ColorPickerPreview` and `ColorPickerFixContrast`.
- **`useColorPicker`**: reads and sets the color from custom parts.

### Value

- **Events**: `onChange` fires while dragging and `onChangeEnd` once an interaction ends.
- **`format`**: what they emit — `oklch` by default, `hex`, `rgb` or `hsl`; `alpha` adds opacity controls.
- **Forms**: `name` submits the value with a form (a hidden input), and a form reset restores the starting color.

### Contrast

Given a background (`contrastWith`), every part shows contrast: the area hatches what fails AA and draws the AA and AAA thresholds across it, tracks hatch and mark them, presets failing AA are hatched, the preview shows the WCAG ratio, and "Fix to AA/AAA" jumps to the nearest passing lightness keeping the hue.

`labels` translates every text it shows or announces.

- **Actions**: `tone="destructive"` marks a destructive action; `cancelLabel={null}` leaves a single action.
- **`onConfirm`**: runs with the dialog open and the button pending; if it throws, the dialog stays open with `errorMessage`.

For dialogs that collect a value or hold a form, render your own dialog with the same hook and call `confirm(value)`.

Labels default to English; pass translations through the label props.

items.name: credit-card
items.title: Credit Card
items.description:
A payment card drawn from its data, to show a saved card or preview one while it's typed.

- **Front**: the chip, the issuer's logo and color, the number padded with `•` and grouped by issuer (Amex 4-6-5), the holder and the expiry.
- **Back**: the stripe, the signature panel and the security code.

### Props

- **Data**: `number`, `name`, `expiry` (`MM/YY`, `MM/YYYY` or digits only) and `cvc` are plain strings. `*` or `x` in `number` hide digits of a saved card.
- **`issuer`**: `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`… — pass it for a saved card; by default it is detected from the number.
- **`focused`**: `number`, `name`, `expiry` or `cvc` highlights the field being typed, and `cvc` turns the card over (Amex keeps its code on the front). With reduced motion it turns without the 3D spin.
- **Size**: its width sets its size (`w-72` by default) and the text scales with it.
- **`labels`**: translates the captions and the accessible name. The card is one `role="img"` ("Visa card ending in 4242, expires 12/28").

Logos for Visa, Mastercard, Elo, American Express, Hipercard, Diners Club, Discover and JCB; other issuers show their name on the theme gray.

Issuer detection and the form's validation (number, expiry, security code) live in the `credit-card-validation` lib, usable without the card. Pair the number field with the `credit-card` mask, which follows the issuer too.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: credit-card-validation
items.title: Credit Card Validation
items.description:
Payment card helpers for forms, without React.

- **`getCreditCardIssuer(number)`**: detects the issuer from the first digits with `credit-card-type` (`null` while ambiguous).
- **`getCreditCardIssuerById`**: reads it from saved card data (`visa`, `Mastercard`, `amex`). Both return the name, valid lengths, digit groups and security-code size.
- **`isValidCreditCardNumber`**: checks the length for the issuer and the Luhn digit.
- **`isValidCreditCardExpiry`**: a real month not yet ended (`MM/YY`, `MM/YYYY` or digits only).
- **`isValidCreditCardCode`**: the code size for the issuer.
- **`getCreditCardNumberLayout`**: the digit groups for what's typed (Amex 4-6-5), used by the `credit-card` mask and component.

items.name: data-grid
items.title: Data Grid
items.description:
A data grid driven by a TanStack Table v9 instance and rendered with react-aria's `Table`, which brings cell keyboard navigation, `aria-sort`, selection, column resizing, row drag and drop and virtualization.

### Table

Create the table with `useTable({ features: dataGridFeatures, ... })`. The exported features cover sorting, filtering with facets, pagination, selection, row expanding (tree rows from `getSubRows`), row and column pinning, ordering, visibility and sizing, with client-side row models. For server-side data (or to show every row), set `manualSorting`/`manualFiltering`/`manualPagination`.

Column `meta` takes:

- **`headerTitle`**, **`headerClassName`** and **`cellClassName`**.
- **`skeleton`**: the cell shown in loading rows.
- **`autoSize`**: the column takes the remaining width (not measured from content).
- **`headerColSpan`**: the header spans the next visible columns on its pin side, e.g. "Quantity" over the amount and its unit. Covered headers take its accessible name and the last one keeps the resize handle.

### Parts

Wrap them in `DataGrid table={table} recordCount={…}`:

- **`DataGridTable`** and **`DataGridPagination`**.
- **`DataGridColumnHeader`**: sort indicator, plus a menu for pinning, moving and visibility when `tableLayout` enables them.
- **`DataGridColumnVisibility`**: a column visibility menu.
- **`DataGridColumnFilter`**: faceted; use `filterFn: "arrHas"`.
- **`DataGridRowSelect`**: a row checkbox, with `enableRowSelection`.
- **`DataGridRowPin`**: pins to the top, or the bottom with `position="bottom"`.
- **`DataGridRowActions`**: a row's actions as `DropdownMenuItem`s behind a menu button, named from `rowLabel`. It doesn't trigger `onRowClick`, and with no items it shows a disabled "no actions" entry.
- **`DataGridRowDragHandle`**: with `onRowsReorder`.
- **`DataGridRowExpand`**: shows `getSubRows` children, indented by depth — or, with `getRowCanExpand` and `DataGridTable`'s `renderExpandedRow`, a full-width details row.
- **`DataGridSelectionBar`**: shows while rows are selected — the count (announced, with how many are on other pages), your bulk actions as children and "Clear selection".

### Rows

- **`onRowClick`**: makes rows actionable (click or Enter).
- **`onRowHover`**: fires when the pointer enters a row, e.g. to prefetch its details.
- **`isLoading`**: shows skeleton rows (`meta.skeleton`) or a spinner.
- **Footer**: `DataGridTable`'s `footerContent` takes footer rows (`DataGridTableFootRow` with `DataGridTableFootRowCell`, `colSpan` to span columns); `tableLayout.footerBackground` tints them.

### Infinite scroll

`DataGridTable`'s `onFetchMore` fires near the end of the loaded rows (`fetchMoreScrollOffset`, in viewport heights), `isFetchingMore` shows a loading row and `hasMore={false}` stops it with `allRowsLoadedMessage`. Works with `isVirtualized`.

### Layout and styling

- **`tableLayout.columnsDraggable`**: lets users drag headers to reorder columns; keyboard users use the header menu's move actions, and pinned columns stay put.
- **`tableLayout`**: also takes `rowRounded`, `headerBorder` and `columnsResizeMode` (`"onEnd"` commits the width on release and draws a line at the pointer while dragging).
- **`tableClassNames`**: adds classes to parts of the table (`base`, `header`, `headerSticky`, `body`, `bodyRow`, `footer`, `edgeCell`).
- **Surfaces**: pinned cells and sticky headers paint `--data-grid-surface` (else `--card` inside a `Card`, else `--background`) and carry `data-pinned`/`data-last-col`.

### i18n

The `i18n` prop on `DataGrid` replaces every built-in string (`{ labels: { sortAscending, rowsPerPage, paginationInfo: ({ from, to, count }) => …, goToPage: (page) => …, … } }`, defaults in `defaultDataGridI18n`). Specific props like `emptyMessage` or the pagination labels still win.

items.description: A menu of actions or options triggered by clicking a button. Supports nested submenus, separators, labels, and a shortcut-display slot for each item.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: emoji-picker
items.title: Emoji Picker
items.description:
An emoji picker with search, skin tones, recently used emoji, custom emoji and a virtualized grid.

`<EmojiPicker />` alone renders a trigger and a popover. Compose `EmojiPickerTrigger` + `EmojiPickerContent`, or `EmojiPickerPanel` in place, from `EmojiPickerSearch`, `EmojiPickerCategories`, `EmojiPickerList`, `EmojiPickerPreview` and `EmojiPickerSkinTone`.

- **Search**: names, keywords and shortcodes.
- **Categories**: a category bar that follows the scroll, plus a frequently or recently used section.
- **Data**: emojibase, fetched once per page from jsDelivr (`dataUrl` to self-host, `locale` for 28 languages) or passed as `data`. `emojiVersion="auto"` hides emoji the device can't draw.
- **Value**: `value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange` hold the native emoji (or `:shortcode:` for a custom one). `selectionMode="multiple"` toggles a list (with `max`), and `onEmojiSelect` fires on every pick, for inserting into text.
- **Keyboard**: focus stays in the search while the arrows move through the grid (a combobox over an `aria-activedescendant` listbox); Enter picks.
- **Persistence**: recent picks and the tone persist in localStorage (`recentStorageKey`, `skinToneStorageKey`; `null` keeps them in memory).
- **Forms**: `name` submits with a native form.

Every string comes from `i18n`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: A placeholder for empty states — no data, no search results, nothing configured yet. Composes an icon/media, title, description, and optional call-to-action content.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: error-pages
items.title: Error Pages
items.description:
Error screens on top of `empty` and `icon-stack`: `NotFound` (404), `Forbidden` (403) and `UnexpectedError`, plus the bare `ErrorPage` for other cases (maintenance, expired link).

Each shows an icon, the status `code` as a small label, the title as the page's `h1`, a description and your `actions` (home, back, support).

- **Layout**: `layout="page"` fills the viewport; `layout="inline"` fills the content area of the app's layout.
- **`UnexpectedError`**: puts a "Try again" button first with `onRetry` (pending while its promise runs). With `error`, it adds a collapsible `ErrorDetails` with the message and stack and a button that copies them — leave `error` out where users shouldn't see it.
- **In the app**: wiring to the router (error and not-found routes), reporting and automatic reloads.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`, or override `title` and `description`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: event-calendar
items.title: Event Calendar
items.description:
A headless-first event calendar: month, week, day, N-day, agenda and resource views, with recurring events, time zones and drag and drop.

- **Recurrence**: structured rules or RRULE strings.
- **Drag and drop**: drag to move, resize and create; keyboard users create through `showDayAddButton`'s per-day buttons.
- **i18n**: with RTL support.
- **State**: a subscribable store (`useEventCalendar`, `useEventCalendarSelector`).

Compose `<EventCalendar>` with `EventCalendarNav` and `EventCalendarContent`, or build your own parts from the hooks. Events are controlled (`events`/`onEventsChange`) or not (`defaultEvents`); `onEventUpdate` accepts, rejects or adjusts each drag.

The nav, view switcher, date picker and "+N more" popover use the registry's react-aria `Button`, `Tooltip`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover` and `Calendar`.

items.name: feature-promo
items.title: Feature Promo
items.description:
A locked feature or an offer on a card: why it matters, what it gives and the call to action.

Inside `FeaturePromo`, put:

- **`FeaturePromoContent`**: with `FeaturePromoTitle`, one or more `FeaturePromoDescription`, `FeaturePromoBenefits` of `FeaturePromoBenefit` (with an `icon` tile) and `FeaturePromoActions`.
- **`FeaturePromoMedia`** (optional): a framed panel — no background images or gradients.
- **`FeaturePromoGrid`** (optional): spans the full width with one to three columns — choice cards, `Item`s with `href` for shortcuts, or cards that explain options.

`variant="brand"` frames the card with a primary → brand gradient border.

`layout="split"` puts the media beside the content and hides it when the card is narrow; `layout="centered"` stacks everything in the middle.

With a `FeaturePromoAcceptance` (a checkbox card), the buttons in `FeaturePromoActions` stay disabled until it is checked — uncontrolled (`defaultAccepted`) or controlled (`isAccepted` + `onAcceptedChange`).
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description:
Layout primitives for building form fields. Pairs with `Label`, `Input`, and friends.

- **`Field`**: the field wrapper.
- **`FieldSet`/`FieldLegend`**: for grouping.
- **`FieldLabel`/`FieldDescription`/`FieldError`**: the usual label + hint + error stack.
- **`FieldSeparator`**: splits a group.
- **`FieldHelp`**: an ⓘ button beside a label or column header that opens help in a popover (touch and keyboard, unlike a tooltip); its required `label` names the subject.
- **`choiceCardClassName`**: the choice-card surface shared by `CheckboxCard` and `RadioCard`; hover uses `accent`. With react-aria the control is the card, instead of shadcn's `FieldLabel` wrapping a `Field`, which would nest labels.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: file-type
items.title: File Type
items.description:
A file type icon: a page with a folded corner and the extension label, in the format's brand or family color (Word blue, Excel green, the GitHub language colors).

- **`type`**: one of 171 extensions (documents, certificates, code, config, archives…), one of 13 families (`image`, `folder`… drawn as a glyph) or any other string (a neutral labelled page).
- **`getFileType()`**: resolves a file name, path, URL or MIME type, including well-known names without an extension (Dockerfile, `.env.local`, `go.mod`, LICENSE) and aliases such as `.cer`. `getFileTypeCategory()` returns the family.
- **`variant`**: `outline`, `solid`, `light` or `mono` (theme gray). A `text-*` class recolors it.
- **`size`**: from `mini` (18px, for table rows) to `xl`; a Tailwind `size-*` class scales the label and stroke with the box (container units).
- **Content**: `label` replaces the text, `glyph` shows the family glyph and `icon` draws a custom icon.

Renders a `span` with `role="img"` named after the type. It has no state, so it works in Server Components.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: file-upload
items.title: File Upload
items.description:
Picks files by dragging them in, pasting them or browsing, and lists them; it doesn't upload.

`FileUpload` holds the `use-file-upload` state — `accept` (`.pdf,.docx`, `image/*`), `maxSize`, `multiple` + `maxFiles`, uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value`/`onChange`), `isDisabled` — and the parts read it:

- **`FileUploadDropzone`**: a react-aria `DropZone`, with keyboard and paste support. By default an icon, title, `description` and a trigger, highlighted with `accent` while a drag is over it.
- **`FileUploadTrigger`**: a `FileTrigger` button.
- **`FileUploadList`**: renders each file with a function.
- **`FileUploadItem`**: a file-type icon or image thumbnail, name, size, optional `progress`, `error`, extra `actions` such as retry, and a remove button that keeps focus in the widget.
- **`FileUploadError`**: a `FieldError` with the validation errors (type, size, count).

Upload progress and retries stay with the app, keyed by file id.

Built-in text is in English; translate labels and error messages with `i18n`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: filter-toolbar
items.title: Filter Toolbar
items.description:
The controls above a list or `DataGrid`, composed from parts that are each controlled (`value`/`onChange`), so every filter maps to a search param.

- **`FilterToolbar`**: lays the parts out, wrapping on narrow screens; its `i18n.labels` reaches every part.
- **`FilterSearch`**: a react-aria `SearchField` that commits the term on Enter and when cleared — and, with `debounceMs`, after the user stops typing.
- **`FilterQuickToggles`**: an outlined `ToggleGroup` for one-press filters.
- **`FilterToolbarActions`**: holds the trailing actions, `FilterSheet` and `FilterRefresh`.
- **`FilterSheet`**: a "Filters" button with the active count, opening a side `Sheet`. Its children are the `Field`s of a draft the app keeps: `onApply` commits it (return `false` to stay open), `onClear` empties it, and Enter applies.
- **`FilterRefresh`**: spins while `isPending`.
- **`FilterChips`**: the applied filters as a react-aria `TagGroup`, each removable with its × or Backspace/Delete, plus "Clear filters". Renders nothing when empty.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: form-wizard
items.title: Form Wizard
items.description:
A form in steps, in a dialog or on a page (a new customer, an onboarding).

`FormWizard` takes `steps` (`{ title, description }` per step) and the current step, controlled (`step`/`onStepChange`) or not (`defaultStep`).

- **Navigation**: it's a react-aria `Form` whose submit is Next, so Enter advances and the current step's fields validate natively (only that step is mounted). Then `onNext(step)` runs — validate or save there (react-hook-form's `trigger`). Returning `false` or throwing keeps the user on the step, and a promise shows Next as pending. Finish runs `onNext` of the last step and then `onComplete`.
- **`FormWizardSteps`**: the `stepper` list. Earlier steps are reachable, later ones only through Next. Titles show when the wizard is wide enough for that many steps; narrower, only the numbers, with the current title under them (container query).
- **`FormWizardStep`**: holds a step's fields; after Back or Next, focus moves to its first field.
- **`FormWizardFooter`**: the progress ("Step 2 of 4", announced politely), `children` before Back (a dialog's Cancel), Back and Next/Finish.

The values stay in the app; with react-hook-form, keep `shouldUnregister` off.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: glance
items.title: Glance
items.description:
A quick piece of information that opens more context one click away — an account notice, a balance, a count of pending items.

`Glance` wraps react-aria's `DialogTrigger` and shares a `tone` (`default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`) with its parts.

- **`GlanceTrigger`**: the compact button — an icon plus `GlanceText` (a `GlanceLabel` caption over a `GlanceValue`), or icon-only with `size="icon"` and an `aria-label`.
- **`GlanceIndicator`**: pins a dot or count to the trigger's corner.
- **`GlanceContent`**: a popover holding a dialog (focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns), laid out with `GlanceHeader`, `GlanceMedia` (an `IconTile` in the tone), `GlanceTitle`, `GlanceDescription` and `GlanceFooter`. Its children can be a function of `{ close }`, to close it from an action.

Tone tints the trigger like `Alert`, with no motion — urgency comes from tone and wording.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A popover that shows on hover or focus instead of click, for previewing content (a profile card, a link preview) without navigating away. Unlike a tooltip, it can contain interactive content.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: i18n
items.title: I18n
items.description:
Puts every registry item in one language with a single optional provider. Without it, items render their own English.

- **`FmaI18nProvider`**: fixed language, the route's, another library's, or its own (`setLocale`, detection, packs loaded on demand). Switching keeps the old language until the new pack loads, so languages never mix. It's a Suspense boundary, with a `fallback` prop for the first load.
- **Precedence**: an item's `i18n` prop, then `overrides`, then the active language, then the fallback, then the item's English.
- **`useFmaMessages`** reads a namespace; **`useFmaLocale`** gives a language selector what it needs.
- **Server rendering**: `loadFmaMessages` and `parseAcceptLanguage` in a route loader. The store is per provider, so requests never share a language.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: i18n-i18next
items.title: I18n I18next
items.description:
Keeps the registry items in i18next's language, so your app's texts and the components switch together.

- **`FmaI18nextProvider`**: goes inside `I18nextProvider` and reads the language, the fallback and the detection from that instance. Each server request can have its own instance.
- **`changeLanguage`**: loads the pack first, then switches i18next, so nothing shows two languages. With `i18n.changeLanguage`, components keep their language until the pack arrives.
- **`useFmaLocale().setLocale`** switches i18next too, so a language selector works the same way.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: i18n-pt-br
items.title: I18n Pt Br
items.description:
Every registry item in Brazilian Portuguese, for `FmaI18nProvider`.

- **Use**: `<FmaI18nProvider locale="pt-BR" locales={{ "pt-BR": ptBR }}>`, or a loader to fetch it on demand.
- **Install**: each translation lands next to its item, in `<item>-i18n/<item>-pt-BR.ts`, including items you haven't added: they only hold text, and compile either way.
- **Update**: install it again after adding items from a newer registry.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: icon-stack
items.title: Icon Stack
items.description:
A layered icon illustration for empty states: three receding cards drawn from `currentColor`, with an optional glyph (`children`) laid flat on the front card.

Pairs with `EmptyMedia`. Decorative: the SVG is hidden from assistive tech, so give the glyph `aria-hidden` too.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: icon-tile
items.title: Icon Tile
items.description:
A square surface that gives icons a consistent footprint.

- **`variant`**: `outline` (bordered), `elevated` (raised chip), `soft` (tinted double container), `solid` (filled) or `frame` (double container matching `Card`). `soft` and `solid` follow `currentColor`, so a text color class retints them.
- **`size`**: from `xs` to `xl`.
- **`radius`**: `default` (clamped to the tile) or `full` (circular).

Renders a `<span>`; wrap it in a `Button` or `Link` to make it interactive.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: A single-line text input, styled to match the rest of the registry. Plain native attributes (disabled, not isDisabled) since it wraps react-aria-components' bare Input rather than a higher-level field primitive.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input Group
items.description: Wraps an Input or Textarea with leading/trailing addons (icons, text, or buttons) inside one bordered container, so the whole group shares a single focus ring and border.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: input-masks
items.title: Input Masks
items.description:
An input-mask system built on Maskito: mask option hooks, formatters and remover utilities for Brazilian documents and common formats.

- **Documents**: CPF, CNPJ, CPF-or-CNPJ, CEP.
- **Contact and payment**: phone; credit card, grouped by issuer (Amex 4-6-5, up to 19 digits).
- **Dates and numbers**: date, date range, date-time, time, decimal.

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input Otp
items.description: A one-time-password / verification-code input rendered as individual boxed slots, backed by a single hidden text input for real typing, paste, and autofill behavior.

items.name: interval-helpers
items.title: Interval Helpers
items.description:
Helpers for inclusive `Interval<T>` spans (e.g. unavailable date ranges), generic over any `T` with a `.compare()` method, such as `@internationalized/date`'s `DateValue`.

`createIsWithinAnyInterval` plugs straight into react-aria's `isDateUnavailable` prop.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.description:
A generic row layout for lists of things — media/icon, title, description, and trailing actions.

- **Rendering**: a `<div>` or, when given an `href`, a real link (hovered with the theme's `accent`).
- **`ItemGroup`**: stacks several with consistent spacing.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: Displays a keyboard key or shortcut (e.g. ⌘K) inline, styled as a small pill. KbdGroup lays out several keys side by side for combos like ⌘+Shift+P.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description:
A form field label.

Pair it with a control via `id`/`htmlFor` rather than passing label text as the control's own children: several toggle-style primitives (`Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroupItem`) render their children inside a small fixed-size box meant for a custom indicator, not prose.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: loading-overlay
items.title: Loading Overlay
items.description:
Blocks interaction while an operation runs. No brand animation: just a spinner.

- **`LoadingOverlay`**: wraps a region. While `isLoading`, its children stay visible under a veil with a spinner and `label` (default "Loading…", announced via `role="status"`), become `inert`, and the region is `aria-busy`.
- **`LoadingScreen`**: the same for the whole app, as a non-dismissable modal (focus held, page hidden from assistive tech, scroll locked) — for operations that must finish before anything else, like saving a status change.

Pass a translated `label` as needed.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: marker
items.title: Marker
items.description: A small inline label used in chat/message timelines — a date separator, a status note, or similar metadata — rendered in muted text with an optional icon.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: masked-input
items.title: Masked Input
items.description:
An `Input` with live Maskito formatting. Works inside a react-aria `TextField`.

- **`mask`**: a preset name (`"cpf"`, `"cnpj"`, `"cpf-cnpj"`, `"cep"`, `"phone"`, `"credit-card"`, `"date"`, `"time"`, `"date-time"`, `"date-range"`, `"decimal"`), a parameterized preset such as `{ type: "decimal", prefix: "R$ " }` or `{ type: "date", mode: "mm/yy" }` for a card expiry (safe to write inline), or custom Maskito options.
- **Presets**: set `inputMode`, `autoComplete` and a placeholder.
- **Value**: `onValueChange` receives the raw value (digits, ISO date, dot-decimal) and the masked text. `value` may be either, so a form can store only the raw value.

For other inputs, such as `InputGroupInput`, spread `useMask(...).inputProps` instead.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description:
An app-style menu bar (File, Edit, View…).

- **Structure**: `Menubar` is a react-aria `Toolbar`, so arrow keys move between menus. Each `MenubarMenu` pairs a `MenubarTrigger` with a `MenubarContent` built on `DropdownMenu`, including submenus (`MenubarSub`).
- **Checkable items**: come from react-aria selection — give a `MenubarGroup` a `selectionMode` (`"multiple"` or `"single"`) and `selectedKeys`/`onSelectionChange`, and its items show a check when selected.
- **Opening**: menus open on press or Enter/Space/ArrowDown. While one is open, hovering another trigger or pressing ArrowLeft/ArrowRight opens the neighbouring menu.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

meta.origin: API of shadcn/ui's Menubar, rebuilt on react-aria Toolbar and the registry's DropdownMenu

items.name: message
items.title: Message
items.description: Layout for one message row in a chat UI — avatar, header, footer, and a content column that aligns to the start or end depending on who sent it. Pairs with Bubble for the actual message content.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: message-scroller
items.title: Message Scroller
items.description:
An auto-scrolling viewport for chat message lists: sticks to the latest message as new ones arrive, and shows a jump-to-end/start button once the user scrolls away.

**Experimental**: it doesn't sit on react-aria-components like the rest of this registry, and `@shadcn/react` is still pre-1.0.

meta.origin: shadcn/ui, style: aria-nova. Built on @shadcn/react/message-scroller, not react-aria-components — upstream hasn't ported this one to the aria base yet.

items.name: native-select
items.title: Native Select
items.description: A styled wrapper around the real, native <select> — use it when you need actual native select behavior (mobile OS pickers, form autofill, no JS dependency) instead of react-aria-components' custom Select.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation Menu
items.description:
Site-header navigation: a `<nav>` list of top-level links and disclosure dropdowns. For app command menus use `Menubar` or `DropdownMenu`.

- **Items**: a `NavigationMenuItem` holds either a `NavigationMenuLink` or a `NavigationMenuTrigger` (a button with `aria-expanded`) plus its `NavigationMenuContent` (a popover).
- **Closing**: Escape or a click outside closes the dropdown and returns focus to the trigger; following a link closes it too.
- **Links**: style plain links like triggers with `navigationMenuTriggerStyle()`, and mark the current page with `aria-current="page"`.
- **Hover**: dropdowns open on press; with `openOnHover` they also open when the pointer rests on a trigger (`delay`, `closeDelay`). That's a non-modal "peek" that leaves focus alone, switches at once to another trigger and closes when the pointer leaves or on Escape. Pressing a peeked trigger keeps it open as a regular dropdown.
- **`NavigationMenuIndicator`**: add it after the list for an arrow that slides under the open trigger.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

meta.origin: API of shadcn/ui's NavigationMenu, rebuilt on react-aria Button, Popover, Dialog and Link

items.name: notification-center
items.title: Notification Center
items.description:
Notifications in the header and on their own page, driven by props and callbacks (no server state).

- **`NotificationMenu`**: the bell — an icon `GlanceTrigger` whose `GlanceIndicator` shows the unread count (also in the button's name). It opens a panel with the recent items, "Mark all as read" (`onMarkAllAsRead`), loading and empty states and a "View all" link (`viewAllHref`).
- **`NotificationList`**: every notification as cards with a read/unread `Badge`, for a page paired with `Pagination`.
- **`NotificationItem`**: an unread dot (or an `icon`), the title — a link when it has `href`, calling `onOpen` — the message, the date (formatted in the `I18nProvider` locale) and icon buttons for `onMarkAsRead` and `onDelete`, described by the title.

Urgent notifications are a `ConfirmDialog` opened with `useDialogPromise`.

Built-in text is in English; override it with `i18n.labels`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: order-summary
items.title: Order Summary
items.description:
What the user is about to confirm before buying: lines, an applicable benefit, discounts, the total and the action.

`OrderSummary` takes the `title`, `totalLabel`, `total` and optional `totalDescription` (values formatted by the app) and the `action` button.

- **Large screens**: a card that sticks while the page scrolls — put it in the side column.
- **Smaller screens**: a bar fixed to the bottom with the total and the action; the total opens the lines in a bottom sheet. Leave room under the page, e.g. `pb-28 lg:pb-0`.

Its children sit in a `description-list`:

- **`OrderSummaryLine`**: `label`, `value` and a `description` under the label — an item, a fee, who the order is for. `tone="discount"` for a negative value.
- **`OrderSummaryOption`**: a benefit behind a `Switch`, such as the account balance, its amount struck through while off.

The total stands apart by size and weight, not only color.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: page-header
items.title: Page Header
items.description:
The top of a page, composed from parts: breadcrumbs, the title with its description and actions, and an optional sub-page nav.

- **`PageHeaderBreadcrumbs`**: an `items` trail whose last entry is the current page.
- **`PageHeaderContent`**: heading on one side, actions on the other, stacked on narrow screens.
- **`PageHeaderHeading`**: `PageHeaderTitle` (the `<h1>`, with an `isLoading` skeleton) and `PageHeaderDescription`. Anything that belongs beside the title, like a status select, goes inside it too.
- **`PageHeaderActions`**: buttons that stretch on mobile.
- **`PageHeaderNav`**: an area's sub-pages, usually a `TabNav`.

Wrap the app in react-aria's `RouterProvider` so breadcrumb and tab links route client-side.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Page-number navigation built from LinkButton — previous/next controls, numbered links, and an ellipsis for collapsed ranges.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: panel-card
items.title: Panel Card
items.description:
A panel on a `Card` — a dashboard chart or table, or one resource and its status (a contract, the current plan) — with a standard header and a body that handles its own states.

### `PanelCardHeader`

- **`title`**: a heading, `headingLevel` 2 by default.
- **`icon`**: shown in a `soft` `IconTile`.
- **`description`** and **`status`**: a `Badge` next to the title.
- **`help`**: opened by an ⓘ button in a popover, so it works with touch and keyboard.
- **`updatedAt`**: a `Date` or timestamp, formatted with `Intl` in the react-aria locale; `isRefreshing` shows a spinner next to it while the content stays on screen.
- **`toolbar`**: a slot for the card's own controls, which wraps below the title on narrow cards.

### `PanelCardBody`

Shows the first state that applies — `isLoading` (skeleton, first load only), `isError` (message plus "Try again" with `onRetry`), `isEmpty` (`Empty`) — or its children. `emptyState`/`errorState` replace the built-in messages (e.g. a missing resource with the action that adds it).

### What goes where

- **Body**: charts, tables, `stat-cards` and `description-list`; problems with the resource go in an `Alert` there, not in the card colors.
- **`CardFooter`**: actions.

`PanelCard`'s `i18n.labels` reaches every built-in text.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: password-input
items.title: Password Input
items.description:
A password field with a show/hide toggle, built on `InputGroup`. Pair it with `password-rules` when creating a password.

- **Toggle**: a button named by `toggleLabel` (default "Show password"; pass a translation as needed) whose `aria-pressed` reports whether the text is revealed.
- **Visibility**: uncontrolled (`defaultRevealed`) or controlled (`isRevealed`/`onRevealedChange`).
- **Input**: the rest of the props go to the input, so it works inside a react-aria `TextField` (label, description, validation) and takes `autoComplete="current-password"` or `"new-password"`.

Hides Edge's built-in reveal button.
items.author: @fma-ds/ds

items.name: password-rules
items.title: Password Rules
items.description:
The rules a new password must follow, each marked pending, met or unmet as the user types — by icon and a screen-reader state label (`stateLabels`), not color alone.

- **`rules`**: takes `PasswordRule` objects (`id`, `label`, `test(value, confirmation)`).
- **`passwordRules`**: builds the usual ones — `minLength(n)`, `maxLength(n)`, `uppercase()`, `lowercase()`, `number()`, `special()`, `match()` against `confirmation` — each taking a `label` to translate it. Defaults to 8+ characters, upper, lower and a number.
- **Neutral start**: rules stay neutral until there's something to judge.
- **Validation**: the pure helpers `evaluatePasswordRules` and `isPasswordValid` share the same rules for form validation.

Give it an `id` and point the input's `aria-describedby` at it.

items.name: payment-card
items.title: Payment Card
items.description:
The payment card screens: the saved card and the form to add one.

### Saved card

- **`PaymentCardDetails`**: draws the saved card (`credit-card`) beside a `description-list` (issuer, last digits, holder, expiry) from the gateway's data (`number` with hidden digits, `issuer`, `name`, `expiry`), with `actions` under it.
- **`PaymentCardRemove`**: the destructive button that asks through a `ConfirmDialog` and runs `onRemove` with the dialog pending, showing an error if it throws.

### Adding a card

`PaymentCardForm` is a react-aria `Form` that lays `PaymentCardPreview` beside `PaymentCardFields` (stacked when narrow). The fields are ready-made react-aria `TextField`s that feed the live preview with their value and focus (the code field turns the card):

- **`PaymentCardNumberField`**: masked by issuer.
- **`PaymentCardNameField`**: `part="first"`/`"last"` split it for gateways that take them apart.
- **`PaymentCardExpiryField`**: `MM/YY`.
- **`PaymentCardCodeField`**: digits, sized by the issuer.

Each takes `value`/`onChange` or `defaultValue`, `name`, `validate`, `isInvalid` and `errorMessage` (for react-hook-form's `Controller`), `label` and `description`. Validate with the `credit-card-validation` lib.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `label`, `placeholder` and `i18n.labels`.

items.name: plan-builder
items.title: Plan Builder
items.description:
Build what the user is about to buy by choosing quantities, with the price in real time: a custom plan with several resources, or a quantity of one item (extra notes, credits).

- **`PlanBuilder`**: lays out the resources and its `summary` (an `OrderSummary`: a sticky card on large screens, a bar fixed to the bottom on smaller ones). `isCalculating` turns every `PlanPrice` (a price formatted by the app) into a skeleton while the app recalculates.
- **`PlanResource`**: a card with `icon`, `title`, `description` and a controlled `Slider` named by `label` (`value`/`onChange`, `minValue`/`maxValue`/`step`, `marks`, `formatValue`, `limit` for stock or quota left, `isDisabled`). A `hint` under the slider says why it stops or is disabled, and an optional `included` accordion lists what comes with it.
- **`PlanResourceAddon`**: an add-on as a child of the resource — a switch with label and description.

The price, debouncing, limits and notices stay in the app.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.

items.name: pricing-plans
items.title: Pricing Plans
items.description:
Choose one of a few fixed plans, then confirm. For a plan built from quantities and add-ons, use `plan-builder`.

- **`PricingPlans`**: lays out the options and an optional `summary` (an `OrderSummary` with the chosen plan and a "Continue" action: a sticky card on large screens, a bar fixed to the bottom on smaller ones).
- **`PricingPeriod`**: the billing period as a segmented toggle that always has one selected (`value`/`onChange`; `PricingPeriodOption` with an `id`, and a `Badge` inside for the saving).
- **`PricingPlanGroup`**: a radio group of `PricingPlan` cards, stacked in one list on small screens and side by side in equal columns once its own width fits them.
- **`PricingPlan`**: `name`, `badge` ("Most popular"), `description`, `price` and `period` formatted by the app, `priceNote` (the equivalent, "R$ 718,80 per year") and `isFeatured` for a brand glow and a `brand` badge (the border is left to the selected plan). The radio is named by the plan and described by its price.
- **`PricingPlanFeature`**: what the plan has; `isIncluded={false}` shows a dash, muted text and "Not included" read before it.

Built-in text is in English; translate it with `i18n.labels`.

- **`SettingsForm`**: a react-aria `Form` that only shows state the app owns, so react-hook-form or any other form state fits: `isDirty` (enables Save and Discard), `isPending` (spinner on Save, `aria-busy`) and `onReset` (adds a Discard button that should restore the saved values).
- **`SettingsSection`**: groups fields under a `title` and `description` (a labelled group) stacked above them, leaving the width to the fields next to an app sidebar. The fields fall into a two-column grid when there's room (container query); `col-span-full` takes the whole row.
- **`SettingsFormFooter`**: a save bar stuck to the bottom of the viewport with a polite status line (no changes / unsaved / saving), optional children before the buttons, Discard and Save.

Warning before leaving with unsaved changes stays in the app, since it depends on the router; use `confirm-dialog`.

- **`label`**: names it above the track.
- **`showValue`**: prints the value (or range) beside it, formatted by `formatValue` ("200 orders") or `formatOptions` (currency, percent — also what screen readers announce).
- **`marks`**: labelled stops under the track (`number` or `{ value, label }`). Clicking one moves the nearest thumb there and fires `onChangeEnd`, while the keyboard keeps using the thumb.
- **`limit`**: caps the value below `maxValue` (stock left, plan quota). The scale and marks still run to `maxValue`, the track above the limit is drawn as unavailable and its marks are disabled.
- **`description`**: under the track, says why, and is read with the value.

items.name: sortable
items.title: Sortable
items.description:
A reorderable list, row or grid (`layout`: `vertical`, `horizontal`, `grid`).

Give it the items as `value` (or `defaultValue`) with `onChange`, and one `SortableItem` per item whose `id` matches `getKey(item)` (defaults to `item.id`) — as static children or a render function.

- **Pointer**: items drag from anywhere; a line marks the drop position.
- **`SortableItemHandle`**: required on every item — the visible grip and its keyboard / screen-reader drag button. Enter starts, arrows pick the drop position, Enter drops; arrows reach it in a vertical list, Tab in a row or grid.
- **`isDisabled`**: pins an item in place.
- **`selectionMode`**: lets several selected items move together.
- **`renderDragPreview`**: replaces the browser's drag snapshot.
- **Events**: `onChange` also gets the moved keys and the drop target; `onDragStart`/`onDragEnd` follow react-aria.

items.name: stat-cards
items.title: Stat Cards
items.description:
Totals above a list or on a dashboard: figures on their own or on cards that are static, pressable, links or filters.

### `Stat`

A label (`StatLabel`), a value (`StatValue`, formatted by the app, with `isLoading` and `isUnavailable` states), an optional `StatIcon` (a `soft` `IconTile`) and a `StatDescription`.

- **`tone`**: `default`, `success`, `warning`, `info`, `destructive` or `muted`; tints the icon and the value.
- **`size="lg"`**: enlarges the value.

On its own, `Stat` has no surface, for several figures inside one card.

### Cards

- **`StatCard`**: static.
- **`StatCardButton`**: runs `onPress`, or opens a dialog as the child of a `DialogTrigger`.
- **`StatCardLink`**: navigates, e.g. to the list already filtered.
- **`StatCardToggle`**: the selectable cards of a `StatCardGroup`, a react-aria `ToggleButtonGroup` that filters a list. `selectionMode="single"` behaves like radios and `"multiple"` like checkboxes, controlled by `selectedKeys`/`onSelectionChange` so it maps to a search param.

`StatGrid` and `StatCardGroup` lay cards out in as many columns as fit, and their `i18n.labels` reach every value inside.

- **Value**: `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange` hold the current step.
- **`StepperItem`**: a tab whose `data-state` is `completed` (before the current step, or `isCompleted`), `active` or `inactive`. `isDisabled` skips it and `isLoading` shows the loading indicator.
- **`indicators`**: swaps an indicator's content per state.
- **`StepperContent`**: panels with the current step's content.

items.name: tab-nav

items.description:
Navigation between the pages of an area that looks like tabs: a `<nav>` of react-aria links where the current page carries `aria-current="page"`.

Unlike `Tabs` there are no panels — each item is a route — so use it for sub-pages and `Tabs` for in-page views.

- **`variant`**: matches the tab styles — `default` (segmented on `muted`, the current page raised) or `line` (underlined).
- **Current item**: when `isCurrent` is set or its `href` matches `TabNav`'s `currentHref` (exactly, or with `matchPrefix` also on sub-paths).
- **`TabNavItem`**: takes an icon before its label; **`TabNavSeparator`** divides groups.
- **Overflow**: when items don't fit, the strip scrolls sideways and keeps the current page in view.

Wrap the app in react-aria's `RouterProvider` for client routing.

items.title: Time Picker
items.description:
A composable time picker: hour, minute, second and AM/PM columns, in a popover or in place.

- **Value**: `@internationalized/date` `Time` objects (`value`/`defaultValue`/`onChange`, `null` when empty).
- **Columns**: `hourCycle`, `granularity` and `periodPosition` shape them.
- **Choices**: `hourStep`/`minuteStep`/`secondStep`, `minValue`/`maxValue` (an overnight window when min > max) and `isTimeUnavailable` narrow them, and a pick moves to the nearest selectable time.
- **`requireConfirm`**: keeps picks as a draft until OK.
- **Keyboard**: each column is an `aria-activedescendant` listbox — arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown and typed digits pick, Left/Right move between columns, Enter commits and closes.
- **Forms**: `name` submits `HH:mm` (or `HH:mm:ss`) with a native form; `isRequired`, `isInvalid`, `isReadOnly` and `isDisabled` work as in react-aria.
- **`useTimePicker()`**: exposes the state inside a picker.

Every string comes from `i18n`.

items.name: use-dialog-promise
items.title: Use Dialog Promise
items.description:
`useDialogPromise<D, V>()`: state and promise for a dialog you render yourself.

- **`open(data)`**: opens it and returns a promise of a `DialogResult<V>` that never rejects — `{ status: "confirmed", value }`, `{ status: "cancelled" }` or `{ status: "dismissed" }` (Escape, outside click, a new open or unmount).
- **`dialogProps`**: spread `isOpen`/`onOpenChange` on any overlay (`AlertDialog`, `Dialog`, `Sheet`), and call `confirm(value)` or `cancel()` from it.
- **Async confirm**: `confirm(async () => value)` keeps the dialog open with `isPending` until it resolves, and open with `error` if it throws.
- **`data`**: holds what `open` passed (kept after closing for exit animations), so the dialog can be its own component that receives the controller.

items.name: use-file-upload
items.title: Use File Upload
items.description:
`useFileUpload`: headless state for picking files, without uploading them.

- **`addFiles`**: validates each file against `accept` (extensions and MIME types, as in `<input accept>`), `maxSize` and, with `multiple`, `maxFiles` (a batch that goes over is rejected whole), and skips duplicates. Without `multiple`, a new file replaces the current one.
- **State**: uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) or controlled (`value`/`onChange`); takes `isDisabled`.
- **Returns**: `files` (`{ id, file }`, where `file` is a `File` or metadata of one already stored) plus `errors` as `{ code, message, file }`, with `messages` to translate them.
- **Helpers**: also exports `formatBytes` and `matchesAccept`.

Progress and retries stay with the caller, keyed by file id.

Based on reui's hook, with its batch, stale-state and StrictMode bugs fixed and its DOM drag handlers left to react-aria's `DropZone` (see `file-upload`).

- **`inputProps`**: spread onto `Input`, `InputGroupInput` or a native input; it carries the masked value, Maskito's ref, and per-preset `inputMode`, `autoComplete` and placeholder.
- **Value**: reports the raw value through `onValueChange`, and accepts a raw or masked controlled value.
- **`TextField`**: reads the value of an enclosing react-aria `TextField`.
